 Cowboys news: Jerry Jones discusses Christian Parker’s role for the rest of 2026
 Here is today’s Dallas Cowboys news
 by Brandon_Loree Nov 18, 2026, 12:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Dallas Cowboys were historically bad on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. Just when you think the bar can’t get any lower, the defense gives up 584 yards of offense—the most allowed at home in franchise history.
 That has raised questions about Christian Parker and his future with the team.
 Jerry Jones: Cowboys ‘talking about’ adjustment to Christian Parker’s role - Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com 
 Does Jerry Jones foresee a change at defensive coordinator for the rest of the season?
 Cowboys Part Ways with 2nd Year Offensive Lineman, Sign Former Buccaneers Guard - Daniel Arwas, Heavy on Cowboys 
 The Cowboys’ track record at developing mid-round offensive linemen takes another hit.
 “The Cowboys have waived OL Ajani Cornelius and signed OL Nick Leverett to the active roster from the practice squad.” DallasCowboys.com’s Tommy Yarish reported on Nov. 17.
 The roster move represents one of the cleaner one-for-one personnel swaps possible, with it very much being one versatile guard-primary offensive lineman in at the expense of another. Since being drafted out of Oregon back in April 2025, Cornelius has only participated on special teams and has yet to record a single snap on offense.
 Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys ‘taking a deep dive, looking at everything’ on defense - Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com 
 It sounded like Brian Schottenheimer was still processing what he saw from his defense on Sunday.
 “I think we got beat pretty good in some man-to-man stuff last night,” Schottenheimer said. “The missed tackles is really what got us. We got to lower our target, we got to wrap up a little bit better, we’ve got to gang tackle a little bit better. Definitely some plays it should’ve been maybe 12, 14, 18-yard plays, and they ended up going for more than that. But in terms of simplifying, that’s definitely a potential solution that we’re talking about.”
 Despite exploring that as an avenue to switch things up defensively, Schottenheimer affirmed that he thinks his players believe in what they’re being coached to do.

 New 2027 Dallas Cowboys Mock Draft Lands LSU Playmaker With Inspiring Story - Randy Gurzi, Cowboys on SI 
 If George Pickens walks in free agency, Dallas might find his replacement in the NFL draft.
 “LSU wide receiver Jackson Harris is starting to see his story be well documented, with an impressive rise from Hawaii to Stanford and Baton Rouge. Harris has been unbelievable this season, and his two-touchdown performance against Texas further improved his pre-draft stock,” Melo wrote. “With the Dallas Cowboys potentially heading for another standoff with George Pickens, this pick could end up making sense.”
